mainTopic: Burned מנחות (the סוטה and wives of כהנים), the differences between כהן and כהנת and between man and woman, and how a כהן's wife's leftover מנחה avoids בל תקטירו
overview: The משנה finishes its list of סוטה cases where her מנחה is burned because she never ends up drinking. It then rules that any woman married to a כהן has her מנחה burned, while a כהנת married to a ישראל has her מנחה eaten. Next it lists differences between a כהן and a כהנת, followed by a longer list of differences between a man and a woman. Those differences cover צרעת, נזירות, a father's authority over his young daughter, and certain punishments. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא explaining how a כהן's wife's מנחה is handled. The קומץ is offered by itself, and the leftovers are dealt with separately. The גמרא asks how burning the leftovers avoids בל תקטירו. It answers first by following רבי אליעזר, who allows burning them as firewood, and then by following רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who has the leftovers scattered on the ash pile.

steps.title: סוטה cases where her meal-offering is burned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of five סוטה cases where the מנחה she brought is burned, because the סוטה process never reaches drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who says 'I am defiled to you,' a woman whose guilt is proven by witnesses, a woman who says 'I will not drink,' a woman whose husband no longer wants to make her drink, and a woman whose husband was with her on the way: in all of these cases her מנחה is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list it started earlier: cases where the סוטה's מנחה is burned. In each case the woman ends up not drinking the bitter water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her מנחה was already brought and made holy, but the סוטה process stopped before she drank. Because it can no longer be offered as intended, it is burned. The five cases cover a confession, proof by witnesses, her refusal, the husband changing his mind, and the husband being with her before she drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am defiled to you': her admission that she sinned, which forbids her to her husband
Witnesses
To make her drink the bitter water
Their meal-offerings are burned, the heading of this list

steps.confusionAlert: The list does not begin here. Its heading, 'these are the women whose מנחות are burned,' comes just before this line in the משנה. That heading is the verdict for every case listed.

phrases.english: A woman who says: 'I am defiled to you,'
phrases.notes: She is confessing that she sinned, so she no longer needs to drink.

phrases.english: and a woman about whom witnesses came that she is defiled,
and a woman who says: 'I will not drink,'
and a woman whose husband does not want to make her drink,
and a woman whose husband had relations with her on the way.
phrases.notes: 'On the way' means on the trip to the מקדש, before she drank.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of burned מנחות, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In each of these five cases the סוטה does not drink, and her מנחה is burned.

steps.title: Meal-offerings of women married to כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a broader rule: any woman married to a כהן has her מנחה burned. A כהנת married to a ישראל has her מנחה eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: All women married to כהנים have their מנחות burned. A בת ישראל married to a כהן has her מנחה burned. A כהנת married to a ישראל has her מנחה eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves past the סוטה cases to a general rule. Whether a woman's מנחה is burned or eaten depends on whom she is married to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman's own family background is not what decides this. Even a regular בת ישראל has her מנחה burned once she marries a כהן. A כהנת, a daughter of a כהן, who marries a ישראל has her מנחה eaten by the כהנים, like any ordinary person's מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Women married to כהנים
A woman from a regular (non-כהן) family
A daughter of a כהן
Is eaten (by the כהנים, after part is offered)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume a כהנת's מנחה is burned just because she is from a כהן family. Here the husband's status decides, not her own lineage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the next question, which is how a כהן and a כהנת differ.

phrases.english: And all women who are married to priests:
their meal-offerings are burned.
An Israelite woman who married a priest:
her meal-offering is burned;
and a priest's daughter who married an Israelite:
her meal-offering is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the topic of burned מנחות from the סוטה cases to wives of כהנים in general.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman married to a כהן has her מנחה burned. A כהנת married to a ישראל has her מנחה eaten.

steps.title: Differences between a כהן and a כהנת: meal-offering and losing status
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how a כהן differs from a כהנת. The first two answers: her מנחה is eaten but his is not, and she can lose her כהונה status but he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between a כהן and a כהנת? A כהנת's מנחה is eaten, but a כהן's מנחה is not eaten. A כהנת can become a חללה, but a כהן does not become a חלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a list of differences between a male כהן and a כהנת and gives the first two. The question is the משנה's own way of introducing the list, not a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first difference picks up from the previous step: a כהנת's own מנחה is eaten, while a כהן's מנחה must be fully burned. The second difference is that a כהנת who has a forbidden relationship loses her כהונה status, but a כהן who does the same keeps his.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between
She becomes a חללה, losing her כהונה status
One who has lost כהונה status

phrases.english: What is the difference between a priest and a priest's daughter?
The meal-offering of a priest's daughter is eaten,
but the meal-offering of a priest is not eaten.
A priest's daughter can lose her priestly status,
but a priest does not lose his priestly status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grows out of the previous rule about a כהנת's מנחה and widens it into a list of differences.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהנת's מנחה is eaten but a כהן's is not. A כהנת can become a חללה, but a כהן does not become a חלל.

steps.title: More differences: corpse impurity and most-holy offerings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list. A כהנת may become impure from the dead and a כהן may not, while a כהן may eat קדשי קדשים and a כהנת may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהנת may become impure from the dead, but a כהן may not become impure from the dead. A כהן eats קדשי קדשים, but a כהנת does not eat קדשי קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the last two differences between a כהן and a כהנת, which completes the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two differences point in opposite directions. The כהן has an extra restriction, since he must stay away from טומאת מת. He also has an extra privilege, since only he may eat קדשי קדשים. The כהנת has neither the restriction nor the privilege.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes impure through contact with the dead
The most holy category of offerings, eaten only by male כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: There are four differences between a כהן and a כהנת: (1) her מנחה is eaten and his is burned; (2) she can become a חללה and he cannot become a חלל; (3) she may become impure from the dead and he may not; (4) he eats קדשי קדשים and she does not.

phrases.english: A priest's daughter may become impure from the dead,
but a priest may not become impure from the dead.
A priest eats from the most holy offerings,
but a priest's daughter does not eat from the most holy offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֶנֶת מִטַּמְּאָה לְמֵתִים וְאֵין כֹּהֵן מִטַּמֵּא לְמֵתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the list of differences begun in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהנת may become impure from the dead and a כהן may not. A כהן eats קדשי קדשים and a כהנת does not.

steps.title: Man versus woman: צרעת and נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts a new list of differences between a man and a woman. It begins with three: a מצורע's mourning signs, making a son a נזיר, and shaving with a father's נזירות קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between a man and a woman? A man who is a מצורע lets his hair grow wild and tears his clothes, but a woman does not. A man can make his son a נזיר with a vow, but a woman cannot do this to her son. A man can bring the קרבנות his father set aside for his father's נזירות when he finishes his own נזירות, but a woman cannot use her father's.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new comparison, man versus woman, just as it compared כהן and כהנת a moment ago. Here are the first three differences.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three cases are הלכות the Torah or tradition gives specifically to a man. The pattern is the same each time: 'a man does X, a woman does not.' These are given as rules, without reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: Lets his hair grow wild and tears his clothes (signs of a מְצוֹרָע)
Makes a vow that his young son will be a נָזִיר
Finishes his own נְזִירוּת using the קָרְבָּנוֹת his father had set aside
The state of being a נָזִיר

phrases.english: What is the difference between a man and a woman?
A man lets his hair grow and tears his clothes,
phrases.notes: This is about someone who is a מצורע. See ויקרא 13:45.

phrases.english: but a woman does not let her hair grow or tear her clothes.
A man can vow that his son will be a נזיר,
phrases.notes: This means a son who is still young.

phrases.english: but a woman cannot vow that her son will be a נזיר.
A man can shave using his father's נזירות offerings,
phrases.notes: His father died after setting aside קרבנות for his own נזירות, and the son uses them to finish his own.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מְגַלַּחַת עַל נְזִירוּת אָבִיהָ.
phrases.english: but a woman cannot shave using her father's נזירות offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new man-versus-woman list on the model of the כהן-versus-כהנת list in steps 3-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a man shows the מצורע's mourning signs, can make his son a נזיר, and can use his father's נזירות קרבנות.

steps.title: Man versus woman: daughters, punishments, and theft
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes the man-versus-woman list: marrying off and selling a daughter, being stoned without clothing, hanging after stoning, and being sold to pay for theft.
steps.simpleTranslation: A father can arrange קידושין for his young daughter, but a mother cannot. A father can sell his young daughter as a maidservant, but a mother cannot. A man is stoned without clothes, but a woman is not. A man is hanged after stoning, but a woman is not. A man is sold to pay for what he stole, but a woman is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה completes its list of differences between a man and a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two cases are about a father's authority over a young daughter, which a mother does not have. The last three are about punishments, where a woman is spared certain treatment that a man receives.

keyTerms.meaning: Arranges קִידּוּשִׁין for his daughter
Sells his young daughter as a maidservant (אָמָה עִבְרִיָּה)
Is stoned (סְקִילָה)
Is hanged after being put to death
Is sold as a servant to pay for his theft

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with two lists: כהן versus כהנת, and man versus woman. In each item, one side has a halacha the other side does not.

phrases.english: A man can betroth his daughter to someone,
but a woman cannot betroth her daughter.
A man can sell his daughter,
phrases.notes: As a maidservant, while she is still a young girl.

phrases.english: but a woman cannot sell her daughter.
A man is stoned without clothes,
but a woman is not stoned without clothes.
A man is hanged, but a woman is not hanged.
phrases.notes: The hanging is done after the stoning, for certain sins.

phrases.english: A man is sold for his theft,
but a woman is not sold for her theft.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the man-versus-woman list begun in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a father can arrange קידושין for or sell a young daughter, and only a man is stoned without clothes, hanged, or sold for theft.

steps.title: How the מנחה of a כהן's wife is offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא explaining the משנה's rule from step 2. A woman married to a כהן has a מנחה that can be neither eaten nor burned whole, so the קומץ and the leftovers are each burned separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: All women married to a כהן have their מנחות burned. How is this done? A woman married to a כהן, whether she is a כהנת, a לויה, or a ישראלית, cannot have her מנחה eaten, because he has a share in it. But it also is not burned whole like a כהן's מנחה, because she has a share in it. Rather, the קומץ is burned on its own, and the leftovers are burned on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that explains exactly how the 'burning' from the משנה's rule in step 2 is carried out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her husband's share makes the מנחה like a כהן's מנחה, so it cannot be eaten. Her own share makes it like an ordinary person's מנחה, which needs a קומץ taken first. So both rules apply: first the קומץ is burned on the מזבח, and then the leftovers are burned separately.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a בָּרַיְיתָא)
Burned completely, the way a כֹּהֵן's מִנְחָה is
The handful taken from a מִנְחָה and burned on the מִזְבֵּחַ
The leftovers of the מִנְחָה after the קוֹמֶץ is taken
A share or part-ownership

steps.confusionAlert: Her מנחה is still a regular מנחה that needs a קומץ. The new twist is only that the leftovers, which are normally eaten, are burned here instead.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
All women married into the כהונה
have their מנחות burned. How so?
A כהן's daughter, a לוי's daughter, or a ישראל's daughter who married a כהן
her מנחה is not eaten,
because he has a share in it.
phrases.notes: 'He' is her husband, the כהן, and a כהן's מנחה is never eaten.

phrases.english: And it is not burned completely,
because she has a share in it.
Rather, the handful is offered by itself,
and the leftovers are offered by themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל הַנְּשׂוּאוֹת לַכְּהוּנָּה מִנְחוֹתֵיהֶן נִשְׂרָפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's rule in step 2 and explains how the burning works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קומץ of her מנחה is burned by itself, and the leftovers are burned separately.

steps.title: Burning the leftovers should violate בל תקטירו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: once a קומץ has gone on the fire, burning the leftovers on the מזבח should be forbidden under בל תקטירו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Apply here the rule: anything whose קומץ has been burned on the fire falls under the איסור of 'do not burn' for the rest of it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Burning the leftovers on the מזבח seems to break a Torah איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that when part of a קרבן has already gone to the fires of the מזבח, burning the rest of it there violates בל תקטירו. Here the קומץ was burned, so how can the ברייתא allow the leftovers to be burned as well?

keyTerms.meaning: Read (apply) here
The fires of the מִזְבֵּחַ
The איסור 'do not burn' on the מִזְבֵּחַ

phrases.english: Apply here the rule:
anything that has a part of it going to the fires
falls under 'do not burn'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיקְּרִי כָּאן: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא מִמֶּנּוּ לָאִישִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא's ruling that the leftovers are burned.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the שיריים are burned on the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קומץ already went to the fire, so burning the rest on the מזבח should violate בל תקטירו.

steps.title: The leftovers are burned as firewood
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי answers that the leftovers are burned as firewood, not as a קרבן, following רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה, son of רבי שמעון בן פזי, said: The כהן burns the leftovers as firewood, following רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The leftovers are put on the fire only as wood, not as an offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תקטירו forbids burning something on the מזבח as a קרבן. Burning the leftovers only as fuel is a different act, so the איסור does not apply. This works according to רבי אליעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Burns, puts up on the fire
As firewood (fuel), not as a קָרְבָּן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, said:
He burns them as firewood,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the leftovers of the מנחה.

phrases.english: following Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the act: the burning is fuel, not an offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning the leftovers on the מזבח counts as offering them, which violates בל תקטירו.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are burned as firewood, which בל תקטירו does not forbid, according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's source: burning as firewood is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says that what may not be burned as a pleasing aroma may still be burned as firewood.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says, you may not burn them on the מזבח as a 'pleasing aroma,' but you may burn them there as firewood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the answer in step 9, showing that רבי אליעזר really allows burning as firewood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads the איסור as covering only burning 'for a pleasing aroma,' meaning as a קרבן. Burning as fuel is outside it. This supports the answer that the leftovers may be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a בָּרַיְיתָא
A pleasing aroma, meaning burning as a real קָרְבָּן

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, the leftovers of a כהן's wife's מנחה can be burned on the מזבח as firewood, which avoids בל תקטירו. The next step asks how the רבנן, who reject this idea, would handle the leftovers.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
For a pleasing aroma you may not burn them,
but you may burn them as firewood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבי אליעזר cited in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That burning the leftovers as firewood is allowed

steps.title: The firewood answer only works for one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 9 relies on רבי אליעזר. The רבנן do not accept his idea, so how would they explain burning the leftovers?
steps.simpleTranslation: That answer is fine for רבי אליעזר, who holds this reasoning. But according to the רבנן, who do not hold this reasoning, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer in step 9 depends on רבי אליעזר's view. It asks how the רבנן, who disagree with him, would handle the leftovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the leftovers were burned 'as firewood' to avoid the problem of בל תקטירו. That idea comes from רבי אליעזר alone. The רבנן do not accept it, so for them the problem from step 8 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one opinion, but not for another)
Line of reasoning
The Sages, the majority opinion
What is there to say? (asking for an explanation)

phrases.english: This works out well for Rabbi Eliezer
who holds this reasoning,
phrases.notes: 'This reasoning' is the firewood idea from step 10.

phrases.english: but according to the Rabbis
who do not hold this reasoning,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּאִית לֵיהּ הַאי סְבָרָא, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן דְּלֵית לְהוּ הַאי סְבָרָא, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from steps 9 and 10 by noting that it only fits one opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The firewood answer of יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer depends on רבי אליעזר. The רבנן reject his idea, so for them the בל תקטירו problem is still unsolved.

steps.title: The רבנן follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the רבנן handle the leftovers the way רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: They treat the leftovers according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to a different תנא, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. The ברייתא in the next step will show what he says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not need the firewood idea, because they can rely on another method for the leftovers. What that method is will be explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They treat them / they do with them
רבי אלעזר, son of רבי שמעון (בר יוחאי)
Son of רבי (so-and-so)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אֱלִיעֶזֶר (step 11) with רבי אֶלְעָזָר ברבי שמעון (this step). The names look almost the same, but these are two different people with two different methods.

phrases.english: For they treat them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the leftovers of the מנחה.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּעָבְדִי לְהוּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different תנא whose view the רבנן can follow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the firewood idea, the רבנן would seem to have no way to deal with the leftovers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's method for the leftovers.

steps.title: The ברייתא: leftovers are scattered on the ash pile
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון has the קומץ offered alone and the leftovers scattered at the place of the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says, the קומץ is offered by itself, and the leftovers are scattered on the place of the ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that is the source for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view the leftovers never go onto the מזבח fire at all. They are scattered on the ash pile, so there is no question of בל תקטירו and no need for the firewood idea. This is how the רבנן can explain the case.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in a ברייתא)
Is offered by itself
Are scattered
The place of the ashes

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, the leftovers are burned on the מזבח as firewood. For the רבנן, following רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the leftovers are not burned on the מזבח at all. They are scattered on the ash pile.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the רבנן can accept the rule about the כהן's wife's מנחה without accepting רבי אליעזר's firewood idea.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
The handful is offered by itself,
and the leftovers are scattered
on the place of the ashes.
phrases.notes: Since the leftovers never go on the מזבח fire, the בל תקטירו problem never comes up.
